items.title: 61531_Juan Tizol oral history interview
items.q: he found out that I was there, and he came by my table -- and he asked me, he said, "I would like to have you in the band so you can match with Miff Mole."

ctx.x: Well, I was in New York, laying off there, and Benny Goodman was at the Astor Hotel, and his trombone player was Miff Mole at that time; he was using only one trombone.

So I came to listen to him, because I would always see Benny Goodman when I could -- he was the best in clarinet, a good musician. So I went over to the Astor one night and I got my little table there, and I listened to him for awhile, and for some reason or another, he found out that I was there, and he came by my table -- and he asked me, he said, "I would like to have you in the band so you can match with Miff Mole." So I said, "Well, that would be fine, but I don't know if I could leave Duke Ellington right…

Well, that was that, and one time when I was in Boston and he happened to be in Boston, too, at the I think it was the Metropolitan Theatre or something, and I saw him. And still, he said, "I would like to have you", and I said something about how much could he offer me because I was making a pretty good salary with Duke Ellington. But I don't know how much I told him, but whatever I told him, he said, "Well, what do you want me to do? Buy you a home?" I said,
